axiom_policy.name: machlib-axiom-ledger
axiom_policy.source: foundations/AxiomLedger.lean: the live knownAxioms and trustedFootprint

cross_checks.check: the axioms counted are exactly knownAxioms
every AxiomLedger headline is a counted theorem
trustedFootprint admits no sorryAx or compiler-trust axiom

excluded_by_a_name_rule_with_a_source_ra.note: Declarations a name or environment rule excludes although Lean recorded a source range for them (expected: macro_rules / elab_rules implementations, `_aux_...`).

outside_environment.note: Tracked .lean files under foundations/MachLib whose module the environment does not contain. Counted as FILES ONLY: nothing elaborated their declarations in this environment, so none of their declarations is counted, and they are never counted by text.

definitions.approved_policy: Footprint within AxiomLedger.trustedFootprint, the declared policy (it includes propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound).
definitions.axiom_audited: Kernel-checked theorems whose transitive axiom footprint (Lean.collectAxioms, what #print axioms prints) was computed and classified against axiom_policy. Equal to kernel_checked by construction; a theorem whose footprint was not computed is unchecked.
definitions.conditional: Footprint within the declared axioms (knownAxioms with trustedFootprint) but not within trustedFootprint: proved on the declared axioms named in the record's conditional_on.
definitions.declarations: Non-auxiliary declarations of every kind (rules.exclusion) whose module is one of MachLib's own, in the environment the imports build.
definitions.kernel_checked: Theorems admitted to the environment by Lean's kernel when `lake build` compiled their module, whose footprint holds no sorryAx, no compiler-trust axiom and only declared axioms = approved_policy + conditional. Importing a module does not re-run the kernel; tools/axiom_ledger/check_kernel_replay.py replays it and is not run here.
definitions.theorems: Declarations of kind theorem (ConstantInfo.thmInfo) = approved_policy + conditional + unchecked. A proof stated with `def` is a definition here (diagnostics.prop_valued_definitions).
definitions.unchecked: Footprint contains sorryAx, a compiler-trust axiom (Lean.ofReduceBool, Lean.ofReduceNat, Lean.trustCompiler, or the `<decl>._native.<tactic>.ax_N` axiom Lean v4.32's native_decide and bv_decide add per use: a compiled evaluation is not a kernel check) or an axiom outside the declared axioms, or was not computed.

exclusion.rule: its name, with any `_private` prefix removed, is an internal detail (Lean's `Name.isInternalDetail`: a component starting with `_` or numeric, or a final `match_N`, `proof_N`, `eq_N`, `omega_N`): auxiliary proofs, macro and elab rules, hygienic names
an auxiliary recursor (`Lean.isAuxRecursor`: casesOn, recOn, brecOn, binductionOn, below)
a name Lean reserves and generates on demand (`Lean.isReservedName`: equation lemmas eq_def / eq_unfold, functional induction, hinj, congruence and match-equation theorems)
an AXIOM matching `AxiomLedger.isCompilerArtifact` (the live function), applied to axioms as `AxiomLedger.liveAxioms` applies it
its parent name is a declaration this rule excludes (`T.below.c`, `T.brecOn.eq`)

Lean recorded no source range for it (`findDeclarationRangesCore?`, the table go-to-definition reads): the elaborator records one for each declaration it elaborates from source text, so one without was generated (`ctorIdx`, `toCtorIdx`, `ctorElimType`, `noConfusionType`, `ofNat`, the `brecOn` of an inductive predicate)

exclusion_notes: The first rule that fires names the reason; a declaration no rule excludes is counted.
A `private` declaration is NOT excluded for being private: `private theorem foo` in module M is `_private.M.0.foo`, written by hand. Its user name goes through the rules like any other name.

`isCompilerArtifact` is a substring test written for axiom names. Applied to every declaration it would drop hand-written theorems such as `geomSum_closed` (`_closed`); diagnostics.compiler_artifact_names_kept lists every non-axiom declaration it matches.
Scope: constants whose module (the environment's module index) is `MachLib`, `MachLib.*` or `CertcomLibm`.
rules.statement_digest: sha256 of the UTF-8 text `machlib-stmt/v1 U<number of universe parameters> <type>`, where <type> is a structural serialization of the stored type keeping constructor shape, constant names with universe arguments, de Bruijn indices and literals, with universe parameters written by position and binder names, binder info and mdata dropped (probe.lean.in, `statementSer`). A representation digest: an alpha-renamed binder does not move it; a mathematically equivalent restatement does.
